note: 'show both grid lines' is written as an interrogative clause, but the words are a command.
'pele yellow' after 'the colour scale' names the colour the scale should be; 'pele' is held as a nominal complement of 'set' instead of a modifier of the clause beside 'yellow'.
'we circulate it wider' — 'wider' is held as a modifier of 'make the colour bar vertical', but it belongs to the clause of 'circulate'.
'pointed down' — 'down' is held as a modifier of 'set', but it belongs with the participle 'pointed', which says how the markers should be.
'bars shorer' — 'shorer' (shorter) is held as the head of a nominal with 'bars' its dependent, but it says how the bars should be and belongs as a modifier of the fragment.
'and drop the legend on the right' is a command, but it is written as a declarative clause.
'to wider' — 'to' is held as a discourse word, but it is the marker of the relation from the clause of 'set' to 'wider'.
'and lose the gridlines' is a command, but it is written as a declarative clause.
'and lay the bars horizontal' is a command, but it is written as a declarative clause.
'to see-through' — 'see-through' is written as the verb of a nonfinite clause, but it is no verb here; it names what the markers become.
'while you're at it, can you make the markers blue circles?' is left untied from 'can you make the line dashed?', but the words relate the two requests.
'there too' is a comment on 'can you make the markers black with a red outline?', but it is left as a fragment tied to nothing.
'also how about logarithmic y scale?' — its words are merged into the one clause of 'how about inverted y axis?' instead of standing as a second fragment.
'we circulate it wider' — 'wider' is held as a modifier of 'make the numbers on the x axis smaller', but it belongs to the clause of 'circulate'.
'on the right' — the relation marked 'on' is started at the clause of 'also show both grid lines', but the words pair 'on the right' with 'at the top' on 'the tick numbers'.
